why: Software reliability metrics (MTBF/MTTR availability). Software engineering; the 2026 syllabus has no unit covering reliability, quality or maintenance metrics.

Software configuration items / SCM. Pure software engineering — not present in TECH1 or TECH2. Note TECH2 Unit 2 has 'Git version control', but this tests the SCM taxonomy of a software project, not Git usage.
Textbook definition of 'system' from systems analysis and design. The 2026 syllabus dropped systems analysis entirely.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
why: Elementary definition question — a large collection of related files is a database. Basic DBMS terminology, which is what this leaf covers.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
why: Asks which of relational / network / hierarchical (tree) is not a logical database structure. That is the classic data-models question this leaf covers.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
why: Enforcing data integrity via constraints rather than triggers/procedures/cursors — relational integrity constraints, which sit with the relational model.
Network topology trade-offs (bus vs star vs ring vs mesh). Data communications, explicitly excluded — TECH2 Unit 2 covers web architecture, not LAN topologies.
Transmission impairments (attenuation, distortion, noise) — physical-layer data communications. No leaf of the 2026 syllabus covers signal transmission.
Multiplexing techniques (FDM/TDM/WDM) — physical-layer data communications, absent from both papers.

Measurable characteristics of an OO design (size, complexity, coupling, completeness, volatility) — these are Pressman's software design metrics, not OOP language mechanics. TECH2 Unit 1 covers classes, inheritance, polymorphism and the like, not design measurement.

OO design heuristic about class responsibility and partitioning a large class — a software design/refactoring guideline from the software engineering syllabus, not a feature of classes and objects as taught in TECH2 Unit 1.
Software quality metric (defects per KLOC as the measure of correctness). Software engineering measurement — no such unit in the 2026 syllabus.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
why: Definition of a database schema as the overall design of the database — core three-schema-architecture terminology in this leaf.
Mapping cardinalities (1:1, 1:N, M:N) describe binary relationships in an ER model — squarely this leaf.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
why: Definition of data integrity, distinguished from data independence and data security — basic DBMS concept vocabulary from this leaf.
Guided vs unguided transmission media (coax, fibre, twisted pair vs atmosphere). Transmission media are explicitly outside the 2026 syllabus.
FDDI LAN standard and its ring topology — legacy data communications/networking, not covered by any unit of TECH1 or TECH2.

Windows NT Server backup-domain-controller administration trivia. Not OS theory (TECH1 Unit 4 is concepts, scheduling, deadlocks, memory, file systems) and not the Linux administration named in TECH2 Unit 2. Also obsolete product-specific knowledge.
Forward engineering vs re-engineering — software maintenance and re-engineering terminology from software engineering, which the 2026 syllabus does not contain.
Distribution of defects across SDLC phases (requirements analysis vs design vs coding vs testing). Software engineering error/defect analysis — no unit of the 2026 syllabus covers the SDLC.
